input.assumptions: <parameter name="assumptions">["No historical actuals are available for this project; estimate is based on story points, backlog description, and typical Angular/API/Stripe/Oracle-migration delivery patterns only.", "1 story point ≈ 6 hours of blended engineering effort (dev+QA+devops) as a rough sizing yardstick, adjusted per task by role mix.", "Backend Developer role has 1.5 FTE (~60 hrs/week/person, ~90 hrs/week combined) — sufficient to cover backend-heavy tasks (RBAC, payments, migration) in parallel with modest overlap.", "QA Engineer is only 0.6 FTE (~24 hrs/week) — this is thin relative to 8 backlog items needing test coverage; QA hours have been capped and concentrated on Urgent/High items, with an assumption noted that Medium items get lighter QA pass.", "DevOps Engineer is only 0.4 FTE (~16 hrs/week) — sufficient only for CI/staging setup and light migration/infra support, not for deep ongoing involvement.", "Frontend Developer is 1.0 FTE (~40 hrs/week) — covers component library, dashboard, invoice UI, login UI, RBAC UI.", "Legacy data migration (PW-8) is treated as the highest-risk/highest-effort item given data volume (400k customers, 2M invoice lines) and is staffed mainly by Backend + DevOps.", "Sprint/calendar duration is not fixed by the client; estimate reflects total effort-hours and cost, not elapsed calendar time.", "Rates and roles are used exactly as given in the rate card; no overhead, travel, or licensing markup beyond the explicit non-labour lines below.", "PDF generation and Stripe account/config assumed already available (sandbox/test Stripe account); only integration engineering effort is estimated."]

input.reasoning: Effort was sized per backlog item using story points as a relative-size proxy, then translated into role-hours based on the nature of each task (e.g., PW-1 CI/staging is DevOps+Backend heavy; PW-2 design system is almost entirely Frontend; PW-3/PW-4/PW-7 are Backend-heavy with meaningful Frontend and QA; PW-8 migration is Backend+DevOps heavy with lighter QA). Role hours were then checked against each role's FTE capacity to avoid over-allocating thin roles (QA 0.6 FTE, DevOps 0.4 FTE) — QA and DevOps hours were kept deliberately lower than a naive points-based split would suggest, with assumptions flagging this thinness. Costs were computed as hours × the exact given hourly rate per role. Non-labour costs cover infra, Stripe sandbox/testing, migration tooling, and a small contingency buffer for third-party dependencies. Priority breakdown allocates each task's total labour+non-labour cost to its priority bucket (Urgent: PW-3, PW-7; High: PW-1, PW-4, PW-5, PW-8; Medium: PW-2, PW-6), summed from the underlying task-level effort model. Given the lack of historical actuals, moderate uncertainty bands are used for scenario percentiles.
